recognize_zh: 視野中散在帶有直線切緣與尖角的紅血球碎片，包括半月形的頭盔細胞（helmet cells）與三角形的三角細胞（triangulocytes），並缺乏中央淡染區，符合裂紅血球（schistocytes）。
features: Multiple red cell fragments with straight cut edges and sharp angular corners
Helmet cells (keratocyte-like fragments with two horn-like projections) and triangular fragments (triangulocytes)
Fragments are smaller and denser than intact red cells, lacking central pallor
Occasional crenated red cells and small dense microspherocytic forms
Only a single platelet seen in this field, raising concern for thrombocytopenia (count should be confirmed)
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a background of normocytic red cells with numerous schistocytes, including helmet cells and triangulocytes with straight edges and pointed ends, as well as occasional microspherocytes and crenated cells. Platelets appear sparse in this field. No agglutination or nucleated red cells are seen. Findings are consistent with red cell fragmentation, as seen in microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (e.g. TTP, HUS, DIC) or mechanical valve hemolysis; correlation with platelet count, LDH, haptoglobin and ADAMTS13 is recommended.

ddx.vs: Bite cells retain most of the cell with a smooth semicircular defect, whereas helmet cells and triangulocytes are small fragments with straight edges and sharp corners.
Echinocytes are intact round cells with evenly spaced short projections, not angular fragments.
HPP shows extreme microcytosis with budding, fragments and elliptocytes in a congenital setting, and does not come with thrombocytopenia.
Sickle cells are elongated crescentic intact cells with two pointed ends rather than angular fragments.
